card.title: Motion of a Freely Falling Body

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Free fall strips motion to its essence: constant acceleration g ≈ 9.8 m/s² downward, independent of mass. With one sign convention held throughout, the equations of motion specialise: a dropped body falls $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ and hits at $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ — a stone from 200 m takes 6.32 s and lands at 63.2 m/s (NEB 2023, g = 10).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Dropped: h = ½gt²; v = √(2gh) - Thrown up: t_up = u/g; h_max = u²/2g; T = 2u/g - Sign convention: up positive → a = −g

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Universality of Free Fall:** All bodies fall with the same acceleration $g \approx 9.8 ext{ m/s}^2$ in vacuum (no air resistance). This is a consequence of the equivalence principle — inertial mass equals gravitational mass. The Apollo 15 hammer-feather drop on the Moon confirmed this.  ·  **Sign Convention Discipline:** Choose one positive direction (e.g., up = +) and use it consistently. For up-positive: $a = -g$, $v = u - gt$, $h = ut - rac{1}{2}gt^2$. The sign of $g$ goes into the equation ONCE — never mix conventions.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Note 1: Take $g = 9.8$ m/s² unless the question says 10 — and say which you used.  ·  Note 2: For a body thrown up, do not put $t = T/2$ anywhere except the top; the position equation is valid for the whole flight.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Stone dropped from 200 m*** — t = 6.32 s, v = 63.2 m/s (NEB 2023, g = 10).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Dropped vs thrown down:** dropped means u = 0; thrown down means u ≠ 0 downward — different v and t.  ·  **Time to top vs time of flight:** t_up = u/g; total flight T = 2u/g — double, by symmetry.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Task 1: Solve five thrown-up problems: $h_{max}$, $t_{up}$, $T$, and return speed, all from $u$ and $g$.  ·  Task 2: Prove ascent time = descent time twice — once by equations, once by the $v$–$t$ graph symmetry.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "v = √(2gh) — the two-line answer for dropped bodies."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A ball is thrown upward at 29.4 m/s. Find the maximum height and total time of flight (g = 9.8 m/s²).** — h_max = u²/2g = 29.4²/19.6 = 44.1 m; T = 2u/g = 58.8/9.8 = 6 s.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: drop numericals (2023). Also expect thrown-up questions (h_max, T) and the energy verification (2020).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Mass never appears:** in vacuum a feather and a hammer fall identically — Apollo 15 proved it on the Moon.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Free fall: a = g ≈ 9.8 (or 10) m/s² downward, independent of mass.  ·  Dropped: h = ½gt², v = √(2gh). Thrown up: t_up = u/g, h_max = u²/2g, T = 2u/g.  ·  Fix one sign convention and keep it through the whole problem.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Galileo's Leaning Tower demonstration (probably apocryphal but conceptually right): two different masses hit the ground together.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: At the top of its flight, a ball thrown upward has: → B  ·  A body dropped from rest falls h in 2 s. In 4 s it falls: → C

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Cleanest Laboratory in Physics Drop anything near Earth's surface and, ignoring air resistance, it falls with the same constant acceleration g ≈ 9.8 m/s² — regardless of mass. Free fall is the equations of motion with a fixed a, and its sign bookkeeping (up positive or down positive) is the examinable skill.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts - **Free fall:** motion under gravity alone (no air resistance, no thrust). - **g ≈ 9.8 m/s²** (often taken as 10 m/s² in NEB numericals) directed **downward** everywhere near the surface; independent of mass, size, material (Galileo's result). - **Sign convention:** choose one positive direction and keep it.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 8:** free fall is $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with a = g — the same three equations. - **To Topic 10:** projectile motion is free fall superposed on uniform horizontal motion. - **To Energy (Unit 5):** conservation of energy verified for a freely falling body — mgh converts to ½mv² (NEB 2020 asks exactly this).…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Up-Down Symmetry (No Air Resistance):** Time up = time down = $u/g$. Velocity at equal heights going up and down are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction. At the top, $v=0$ but $a=g$ downward — zero velocity does NOT mean zero acceleration.  ·  Note 3: Impact-speed questions: $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ works even when $t$ is unknown — fastest route.  ·  Note 4: Two-body fall problems: write $y_1(t)$ and $y_2(t)$ with one origin; separation is their difference — accelerations add no relative change if both are $g$.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Verified PYQ: dropped stone numerical (2023, 3m). The 2020 energy-verification question uses the same motion.  ·  "Free fall forgets the mass — only g remains."  ·  Why does a crumpled paper fall slower than a flat sheet?

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Task 3: Solve a mixed case: thrown DOWN from a height with initial speed (find $t$ and $v$ at ground).  ·  Task 4: Solve a lift problem (coin dropped in an ascending/descending lift) in both frames.  ·  Task 5: Derive $h = \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$ from the $v$–$t$ area for a dropped body and verify the 1:3:5 pattern for $n = 1, 2, 3$.
